topic: How are link budgets affected when prioritizing high-revenue services versus navigation safety margins in dynamic scheduling?
consensus_response: Dynamic scheduling faces a trade-off between maximizing revenue service bandwidth and ensuring navigation safety margins. High-revenue service prioritization increases interference and degrades link quality, impacting both safety and service reliability.  This requires dynamic adjustments to modulation, coding, and power control to optimize bandwidth allocation and mitigate interference, ensuring both service quality and safety margin are met.  Network-level analysis like SINR is crucial for this optimization.
reference_context: High-revenue services demand increased bandwidth and higher transmit power, leading to reduced receiver sensitivity and increased interference.  To mitigate this, dynamic scheduling prioritizes high-revenue services, potentially compromising safety-critical operations. This creates a trade-off: greater bandwidth allocation for revenue services can lead to reduced link budget margins, impacting the reliability of safety-critical operations.
